description.narrative:
The proposed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Cities Improvement Project will help provincial and city governments of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province (KPK) to improve the livability of five cities (Abbottabad, Kohat, Mardan, Mingora, and Peshawar) by (i) expanding physical investments in urban water, sewerage, solid waste disposal, and green infrastructure; (ii) providing institutional support to improve service delivery and the performance of municipal companies, and (iii) promoting gender-friendly municipal services through empowerment and capacity development. The project will benefit up to 3.5 million people in the five target cities of KPK. The project supports the government's development priorities, established in (i) the KPK Water Act (2020), (ii) the amended Local Government Act (2019), (iii) the Integrated Water Resource Management Strategy for KPK, and (iv) Pakistan's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
This is the first urban project being categorized as Gender Equity Theme (GEM) in Pakistan. This is also the urban project that is contributing most to ADB's commitment to Climate Financing with over $ 30 million climate adaptation and $ 100 million climate mitigation in 2021/2022. The proejct is being prepared with ADB's first project readiness financing (PRF) approved in March 2019. Thanks to PRF, the government has achieved a high level of project readiness including (i) 100% completion of detailed engineering designs (DEDs), (ii) 100% preparation of draft bidding documents and consultants TORs and approval by the provincial government, (iii) preparation and disclosure of over 30 safeguard documents based on DEDs, (iv) establishment of fully staffed core PMU with additional recruitments to follow, (v) issuance of 7 procurement packages worth over $300 million or about 75% of ADB financing as advance procurement. -

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Women's role in urban development increased Indicator: At least 100 WBDC business development trainees provided with materials and technical training have set up their own businesses Progress/Status: A survey conducted and data analysis has been done for the needs assessment with 100 Women in Kohat for Women business development Center. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Women's role in urban development increased Indicator: At least 100 women entrepreneurs have established their green enterprises with the material and business under the Community Incentive Fund established by the project Progress/Status: Substantial preparatory work has been completed to facilitate the achievement of this target. All required documentation for the launch of the CIF has been finalized, including the Operational Manual, application forms tailored for three distinct categories of businesses, and a comprehensive advertisement strategy. Additionally, the CIF Committee has been constituted, and a Management Information System (MIS) for processing online applications has been developed. These documents and tools have been reviewed and approved by the Project Management Unit (PMU) and subsequently shared with the Asian Development Bank (ADB), which has also formally approved the CIF framework. The official advertisement and launch of the program are scheduled for the 1st quarter (Q1) of 2026. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Women's role in urban development increased Indicator: At least 55 female beneficiaries of the project's scholarship program earned university degrees in the fields related to urban water supply and sanitation Progress/Status: The second batch of the remaining 25 scholars for the one-year master's degree scholarships has been sent in Q1 2026.
Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient and gender-friendly urban infrastructure improved Indicator: Cumulative sewage treatment capacity of 30,000 cubic meters daily achieved with construction of two new treatment plants Progress/Status: This will be initiated after completion of CW03 and CW04. Data Source: Project progress reports, WSSC and city government records, and project records (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: An estimated 150 DMAs with SCADA system for water supply commissioned Progress/Status: All lots related to SCADA have been awarded and works are in progress. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: At least 50% of the target population reached through consultations and awareness raising campaigns are women Progress/Status: A comprehensive Behavior Change Communication (BCC) Strategy, along with City Action Plans and the KPCIP Action Plan, has been developed for the five participating KPCIP cities. To support the effective field-level implementation of the BCC activities, the recruitment process for a specialized firm under the Reforms Section has been formally initiated. Terms of Reference (ToRs) for this assignment have been developed and submitted for necessary approvals. While the procurement process is underway, each of the five City Implementation Units (CIUs) has proactively conducted awareness-raising and community consultation sessions within their respective localities. These sessions aim to promote key messages on safe water use, sanitation, and hygiene practices, while also collecting community feedback to inform and refine ongoing interventions. Efforts are being made to ensure meaningful participation of women and girls in these sessions, in line with the project's gender inclusion targets.
Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: Gender-inclusive HR policies and procedures developed and adopted for five WSSCs Progress/Status: A revised draft of the gender-inclusive HR policies and procedures document has been submitted by IRCB following the initial review. Subsequently, a meeting was held with the concerned consultant from IRCB to further clarify the purpose, scope, and specific requirements of the document in alignment with the indicator. The draft is currently under detailed review for finalization. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: Performance/service benchmarks for key urban services, with sex-disaggregated targets approved for five WSSCs Progress/Status: A comprehensive set of performance and service benchmarks—incorporating sex-disaggregated targets—has been formulated as an integral component of the gender-inclusive human resource policies of the five WSSCs. The final draft of the benchmark document has been submitted and is currently under review for formal approval. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: At least 20% of board members in each WSSC are women Progress/Status: The boards of WSSCs were dissolved. New boards have been formed, but 20% female representation was not ensured with current at 10.63%. A reminder for enhancement of women members to at least 20% has been shared with all WSSCs through PMU. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: Nonrevenue water reduced to 30% of total water produced Progress/Status: The performance indicators will be achieved after completion of civil works packages CW-02 and CW-04. The implementation of non-revenue water management will be initiated following the completion of the new water distribution network and rehabilitation of the existing network in four Project cities of Abbottabad, Kohat, Mingora and Peshawar under two Civil Works (CW) procurement packages - KPCIP/ CW-02 & KPCIP/CW-04. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient and gender-friendly urban infrastructure improved Indicator: 1.6 km2 of gender-friendly and climate resilient urban spaces and parks established Progress/Status: Contracts have been awarded for all lots of CW01 and letters of commencement were issued in October 2022. Civil works are underway of all the awarded works.
CW-01-Lot 3- Ring Road Green Belt and N-45 National Highway, Mardan: This sub-project has been terminated. ADB granted approval for termination. Data Source: Project progress reports, WSSC and city government records, and project records (biannual reporting) Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2027 Target value: 1.6 km

Data Source: Project progress reports, WSSC and city government records, and project records (biannual reporting) Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: 0 km Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: 0 km Target year: 2027 Target value: 156 km

Data Source: Project progress reports, WSSC and city government records, and project records (biannual reporting) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: 550 Target year: 2027 Target value: 1200+550

The bidding documents are ready following cabinet approval the tender would be floated. Output: Institutional capacities of gender-inclusive urban service providers strengthened Indicator: New tariff scheme formulated and adopted by WSSCs Progress/Status: IRCB consultants have proposed a tariff structure which has been reviewed by PMU and WSSC's, IRCB is incorporating comments provided by PMU and WSSC's will be finalized in Q1 2026. Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: Women's role in urban development increased Indicator: A WBDC in Kohat constructed and one technical training institute for girls in Peshawar upgraded Progress/Status: The construction work for the Women Business Development Center (WBDC) in Kohat is currently in progress. In alignment with the project's gender-responsive objectives, the operationalization of the WBDC has also been advanced. Following multiple internal reviews, the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Specialist finalized the operational plan for the Multi-Model Women Business Development Center (MMWBDC), as per the Terms of Reference (TORs) developed by the Gender Section of PMU-KPCIP.
A presentation on the proposed operational plan was conducted by the PPP Specialist during a meeting held at PMU-KPCIP on 18th April 2025. Subsequently, a follow-up meeting was convened on 27th May 2025 to further deliberate and explore additional implementation options. As a result, seven distinct operational models have been proposed to guide the functionalization of the center.
Currently, the evaluation and selection of the most suitable operational model—based on contextual feasibility, sustainability, and alignment with gender empowerment goals—is underway. The final model is expected to be selected and approved in Quarter 1 of 2026.
Data Source: WSSC, GOKP, project progress reports (biannual reporting) Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y
